text: Misfires were detected on more than one cylinder.
hint: Check the single-cylinder misfire codes stored with it; common causes are worn plugs, coils, vacuum leaks or Valvetronic/injector problems.
notes: The 29CC-29D2 misfire numbering is shared by the E9x petrol engine computers, not only the N52 DME. Snap-on source is an E90 with N43.

text: The engine computer detected misfiring on cylinder 1.
hint: Swap the cylinder 1 ignition coil with a neighbour and see if the fault follows it; spark plug, injector and vacuum leaks are other common causes.
notes: The 29CC-29D2 misfire numbering is shared by the E9x petrol engine computers, not only the N52 DME.

text: The engine computer detected misfiring on cylinder 2.
hint: Swap the cylinder 2 ignition coil with a neighbour and see if the fault follows it; spark plug, injector and vacuum leaks are other common causes.
notes: The 29CC-29D2 misfire numbering is shared by the E9x petrol engine computers, not only the N52 DME.

text: The engine computer detected misfiring on cylinder 3.
hint: Swap the cylinder 3 ignition coil with a neighbour and see if the fault follows it; spark plug, injector and vacuum leaks are other common causes.
notes: The 29CC-29D2 misfire numbering is shared by the E9x petrol engine computers, not only the N52 DME.

text: The engine computer detected misfiring on cylinder 4.
hint: Swap the cylinder 4 ignition coil with a neighbour and see if the fault follows it; spark plug, injector and vacuum leaks are other common causes.
notes: The 29CC-29D2 misfire numbering is shared by the E9x petrol engine computers, not only the N52 DME.

text: The engine computer detected misfiring on cylinder 5.
hint: Swap the cylinder 5 ignition coil with a neighbour and see if the fault follows it; spark plug, injector and vacuum leaks are other common causes.
notes: The 29CC-29D2 misfire numbering is shared by the E9x petrol engine computers, not only the N52 DME.

text: The engine computer detected misfiring on cylinder 6.
hint: Swap the cylinder 6 ignition coil with a neighbour and see if the fault follows it; spark plug, injector and vacuum leaks are other common causes.
notes: The 29CC-29D2 misfire numbering is shared by the E9x petrol engine computers, not only the N52 DME.

text: Fuel mixture control for cylinders 1-3 is out of range, usually because the engine is running lean.
hint: Common causes are unmetered air (crankcase vent valve, oil filler cap, intake gaskets), a weak fuel supply or a dirty air-mass sensor.
notes: BMW splits the inline-six into two banks for mixture control: bank 1 = cylinders 1-3, bank 2 = cylinders 4-6.

text: Fuel mixture control for cylinders 4-6 is out of range, usually because the engine is running lean.
hint: Usually appears together with 29E0; look for vacuum leaks (crankcase vent valve is a common cause) before replacing sensors.
notes: Bank 2 = cylinders 4-6 on the inline-six.

text: Fuel mixture adaptation for cylinders 1-3 has reached its limit (reported generically as P0172).
hint: Often logged together with 2A2F and the air-mass code 2D06; check for intake leaks and the air-mass sensor.
notes: Both sources agree it is a mixture-control code; the bank assignment comes from the P-code pairing in the e90post thread title. The 525xi source is an E60 with the same N52 engine family.

text: Fuel mixture adaptation for cylinders 4-6 has reached its limit (reported generically as P0175).
hint: Usually seen with 2A2E; check for intake leaks and the air-mass sensor.
notes: Bank assignment from the P-code pairing in the e90post thread title.

text: The Valvetronic eccentric shaft position sensor reports values that do not make sense.
hint: Unplug the eccentric shaft sensor under the valve cover and check for engine oil in the connector; an oil-soaked harness (and sometimes DME connector) is a known cause.

text: The Valvetronic eccentric shaft position signal is implausible.
hint: Same known cause as 2A37: oil leaking past the eccentric shaft sensor gasket into its wiring; the valve cover gasket is often leaking too.

text: The Valvetronic motor is moving sluggishly or its circuit appears open.
hint: Check the Valvetronic motor wiring and connector; a failed or seized Valvetronic motor (or a sticking eccentric shaft) is the common cause.
notes: Also seen written as 002A38.

text: The Valvetronic servo motor is not getting a proper power supply.
hint: Usually causes limp mode. Check battery/charging voltage and the Valvetronic power feed (relay, fuse, wiring) before replacing the motor.
notes: One thread pairs it with the generic code P1056 (VVT supply voltage).

text: Activation fault on the intake VANOS solenoid circuit.
hint: Check the intake VANOS solenoid connector and wiring, then the solenoid itself.
notes: Source is a 2011 328xi with N51.

text: The intake VANOS (camshaft timing) unit is stiff or mechanically stuck.
hint: Common cause: a sticking or dirty intake VANOS solenoid; BMW's service bulletin also called for a DME software update on affected cars. Check oil level and condition too.

text: The exhaust VANOS (camshaft timing) unit is stiff or mechanically stuck.
hint: Common cause: a sticking or dirty exhaust VANOS solenoid; swapping intake and exhaust solenoids shows whether the fault follows the part.

text: The intake camshaft position relative to the crankshaft is outside the expected range.
hint: Common causes are a sticking intake VANOS solenoid or low/dirty oil; on high-mileage engines also consider timing chain stretch.

text: The exhaust camshaft position relative to the crankshaft is outside the expected range.
hint: Common cause is a sticking exhaust VANOS solenoid; low oil level and timing chain wear are other possibilities.

text: The intake camshaft sensor signal cannot be used to synchronise the engine.
hint: Can cause long cranking or no-start. Check the intake camshaft sensor and its wiring; a stuck intake VANOS solenoid can also set it.

text: The exhaust camshaft sensor signal cannot be used to synchronise the engine.
hint: Check the exhaust camshaft sensor and wiring; a stuck exhaust VANOS solenoid is another known cause.

text: The engine computer reports a problem with the crankshaft position sensor signal.
hint: Check the crankshaft sensor connector and wiring at the back of the block before replacing the sensor.

text: Activation fault on DISA intake-manifold flap servo motor 2.
hint: Check the DISA valve connector and wiring, then the DISA valve itself before considering the intake manifold.
notes: Also seen written as 002AA9.

text: The DME's self-test of the DISA variable intake system failed.
hint: Common cause: a worn or broken DISA valve (flap rattling or stuck); symptoms include rough idle and low power.
notes: X5 source is an E70 with the same N52 family.

text: The DME's self-test of DISA variable intake system 2 failed.
hint: Common cause: a failed DISA valve; owners often find both valves worn when one code appears.

text: The pre-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 1-3 failed its plausibility/system check.
hint: Check for exhaust leaks ahead of the sensor and intake air leaks before replacing the sensor.
notes: Meaning from motorschmiede (German, not engine-specific); the e90post thread confirms the code on an E90.

text: The pre-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 1-3 has reached its control/trim limit.
hint: Check for intake or exhaust leaks; an ageing sensor is another common cause.
notes: Single source, not engine-specific; also reported on N52 in https://www.bimmerfest.com/threads/help-error-codes-2c31-2c32-2c2b-2c6c-n52.1408721/

text: The post-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 1-3 reports a trim/plausibility problem.
hint: The DME could not correct the front sensor using the rear one; check for exhaust leaks and the front sensor as well as the rear sensor.

text: The post-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 4-6 reports a trim/plausibility problem.
hint: Same diagnosis as 2C7E but for the rear sensor on cylinders 4-6.
notes: z4-forum source is a Z4 (E85/E86) with the same N52 DME family.

text: The post-catalyst oxygen sensor for cylinders 4-6 shows no activity (generic P0160).
hint: Test the sensor heater and signal wiring before replacing the sensor.
notes: Meaning from the P0160 pairing in the YouTube title; 1addicts source is an E82 128i (N52).

text: The air-mass (intake air metering) system reports implausible values.
hint: Common cause is unmetered air (vacuum leak, crankcase vent valve, intake boot) rather than the air-mass sensor itself.

text: The air-mass sensor signal is faulty or out of range.
hint: Check the air-mass sensor connector and for intake leaks; replace the sensor if wiring is good.
notes: Also seen written as 002D0F.

text: Power management in the engine computer logged an on-board electrical system (voltage) fault.
hint: Check battery condition and alternator output; one video ties it to alternator over-voltage.

text: Power management in the engine computer logged a battery/voltage problem.
hint: Often follows a flat battery; check battery, charging and loose power connections (one owner found a loose junction-box wire).

text: The electric coolant pump is not running at the speed the engine computer asked for.
hint: Usually the electric water pump is failing; low coolant or air in the system can also set it. Bleed the system before condemning the pump.

text: The engine computer has switched the electric coolant pump off.
hint: Commonly means the electric water pump has failed (e.g. drawing too much current); replacing pump and thermostat together is common practice.

text: The electric coolant pump is running in reduced-power mode.
hint: Early sign of a failing electric water pump; also check coolant level and air in the system.

text: The engine computer cannot communicate with the electric coolant pump.
hint: Check the pump's connector (corroded pins are common) and the data wire; otherwise the pump is likely faulty.

text: Communication with the electric coolant pump failed, possibly due to its power supply.
hint: Check the pump's fuse, power and ground wiring and connector; if they are good, the pump is the usual culprit.

text: The engine computer is not getting a valid signal from the intelligent battery sensor (IBS).
hint: Check the IBS on the battery negative terminal and its wiring; it often appears after battery work.

text: The intelligent battery sensor (IBS) reports an internal function fault.
hint: Check the IBS connector and wiring at the battery negative terminal before replacing the sensor.

text: Signal transmission from the intelligent battery sensor (IBS) is faulty.
hint: Check the IBS data wire and connector at the battery negative terminal.

text: The engine computer has lost communication with the intelligent battery sensor (IBS).
hint: Check the IBS and its wiring; a weak battery or poor connection at the terminal is a common trigger.

text: The engine computer cannot communicate properly with the alternator.
hint: Often logged after battery or alternator work; check the alternator's data connector and wiring, then the alternator voltage regulator.
notes: 5series.net source is an E60 (same N52 DME family).

text: Fault with the oil condition (level/quality) sensor.
hint: Check the sensor's connector and wiring at the bottom of the oil pan; the sensor itself fails often. Verify oil level with a manual reading since the dash level reading will be unreliable.
notes: Also seen written as 0x2E9F.

text: The map-controlled (electrically heated) thermostat has a mechanical fault, e.g. stuck open.
hint: Usual fix is a new thermostat; engine running cold or slow warm-up is the typical symptom.
notes: obdthink page only lists 2EF4 by title in its related-articles list.

text: Activation fault on the map-controlled thermostat's heating element.
hint: Check the thermostat connector and wiring; if the code returns after a new thermostat, suspect the harness.

text: Activation fault on the electric radiator cooling fan.
hint: Check the fan's fuse and large power connector; the fan motor or its built-in controller is the usual failure.

text: The electric cooling fan failed its self-diagnosis.
hint: A fan stuck at full speed is a typical symptom; the fan/controller assembly usually needs replacing.
